work.title: Tel jour telle nuit
work.movement: VII–IX: Je n’ai envie que de t’aimer; Figure de force brûlante et farouche; Nous avons fait la nuit

version.value: Songs 7, 8 and 9 of the nine-song cycle for voice and piano, on the third side of the set.
version.note: The Internet Archive item lists the three songs on this side in this order. The dealer’s supplement lists the nine songs and says the cycle occupies three sides. The printed edition used is not named.

performers.note: The Internet Archive item credits Pierre Bernac and Francis Poulenc and lists baritone and piano; the March 1948 supplement names both and cites “the composer’s participation in the recording”.

date.note: The set was listed as an import by March 1948. The Internet Archive metadata for the other two sides of the set gives “1948-12”, which is later than that listing and so cannot be the date of recording or first issue.

place.note: No source consulted names the studio.

label.note: The supplement lists two 12-inch imported records, Nos. G-DB6383/4.

catalogue.value: DB 6384, side 1 (the cycle’s first six songs are on the two sides of DB 6383)
catalogue.note: The Internet Archive label data read “D.B.6384” for this side, with Dans le jardin d’Anna on the other; the other transfers of the set read “D.B.6383”.

matrixTakeSides.value: 2EA 11110-1 (this side); the reverse, Dans le jardin d’Anna, is 2EA 11131
matrixTakeSides.note: From the item descriptions of the two transfers.

credits.value: George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project (Internet Archive); disc from the Goodfriend collection
credits.note: The item description names the engineer’s firm and lists the collections georgeblood and 78rpm_goodfriend.

date.value: Not stated; the item was made public on 1 July 2024
date.note: The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

processing.value: Four stylus sizes were tried; the preferred version was equalised with turnover 375 Hz and roll-off −12 dB, and copied under the friendlier file name.
processing.note: As stated in the item description. The published MP3 is the Internet Archive derivative of that file.

digital.format: Internet Archive derivative MP3 from a FLAC transfer

composition.value: Poulenc died in 1963, so the music is in copyright in the EU under the life-plus-70 term, which runs to the end of 2033; national wartime extensions, which can lengthen the term for older works in France, were not assessed. The poems are by Paul Éluard, who died in 1952; rights in the poems are not assessed here.
composition.note: Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording. The dates of death are those given in the cited note; the United States status of the music and the poems is not established here.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; listed as an import by March 1948.
recording.note: The United States status of a recording made in France in the 1940s is not established.

rights.creditLine: Francis Poulenc, Tel jour telle nuit, FP 86, songs 7–9. Pierre Bernac, baritone; Francis Poulenc, piano. HMV DB 6384, listed as an import by March 1948. Transfer by George Blood, L.P., for the Great 78 Project; Internet Archive item 78_tel-jour-telle-nuit-no-3_pierre-bernac-francis-poulenc-poulenc_gbia0553972a. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established.
